Subject: Heliotropic - multi-year anchor & staged uplift approval request

Team,

Quick summary / ask: Heliotropic (SaaS provider in chronic care) is pushing for a 3-year committed purchase to lock pricing and secure capacity for a regional launch. Proposal asks: a price lock for the first 18 months, then a staged uplift schedule (Year 2: +6%, Year 3: +8%), and a renewal-protection clause that limits first renewal increase to +10% of the final contracted rate (they also want no mid-contract True-Up unless usage grows by >15%). They are asking for a 20% list discount up front and want an early-exit option with a declining fee schedule. TCV ~ $4.2M over 3 years.

Why this is special: the staged uplift model (0% -> 6% -> 8%) plus the renewal cap and limited true-up are non-standard and would be visible precedent for other large healthcare customers. We need exec sign-off on: 1) the staged uplift allowance, 2) the renewal cap at +10% (or counter), and 3) approval for the proposed early-exit fee schedule.

Attachments: term_sheet_heliotropic_v3.pdf, deal_summary_heliotropic.xlsx (pricing scenarios + margin impact).

Requested timeline: please approve (or provide required edits) by EOD Fri 10/29 so we can close before their board meeting on 11/5.

Key ask bullets:
- Approve staged uplift (0% / 6% / 8%)?
- Approve renewal protection cap (proposed +10%)?
- Approve early-exit fee schedule as drafted?

I'll be available on short notice for a call if anyone wants to walk models.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive 
Redwood Inference
(t) 415-555-0183

--
References: Heliotropic contact: Samir Gupta <samir@heliotropic.health>. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HS-54219

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Heliotropic - multi-year anchor & staged uplift approval request

Tessa — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying Qs before I greenlight anything:

1) Usage trajectory: do we have the month-by-month forecast for year 1 vs year 2? The uplift schedule materially depends on expected growth. Please paste the forecast from the attached spreadsheet (I couldn't open Excel on my phone).

2) SLA / capacity commitments: are they asking for any SLA exceptions (99.9% vs standard 99.5%) or dedicated pool clauses? If they're asking for higher SLOs we need to quantify cost.

3) True-up mechanics: they propose "no mid-contract True-Up unless +15% usage" — I want this changed to an annual true-up that is revenue-neutral (true-up reconciles actual to committed). No one-off carveouts.

4) Escrow / price-lock guarantee: we can consider escrow for a portion of the TCV to backstop the price-lock, but that will require legal/finance coordination.

5) Margin impact: finance: Jordan, see the deal summary — current projected gross margin on committed run-rate is ~36% with the proposed discounts and staged uplift. If we move the renewal cap to +12% instead of +10% it improves long-term margin but weakens the customer ask.

Tessa — paste the underlying monthly forecast and confirm whether they require a dedicated capacity pool (Redwood Dedicated) or are comfortable with hosted with capacity guarantees.

All — I reviewed the attached financials and had a quick call with Samir this morning. A couple of datapoints:

- Heliotropic is planning a Q1 2027 regional launch that requires stable capacity and predictable unit economics for their product team. They are a strategic reference in the chronic care cohort and are being courted by two other infra providers. Losing this deal is a near-term competitive risk and could stall a bigger multi-region rollout.

- Forecast: Year 1 ARR ramp from 0 to ~120k active users by month 12; Year 2 expected +45% usage growth; Year 3 steady +20%. I've uploaded a redline of the term sheet with suggested language to preserve Redwood's upside: term_sheet_heliotropic_v3_redline.pdf. Key recommendations:
  * Keep staged uplift as requested (0%, 6%, 8%) but require an annual true-up reconciliation tied to committed minimums.
  * Accept renewal-protection clause but tighten the renewal cap to +12% rather than +10% given the long time horizon and forecast uncertainty — this buys margin for Redwood while remaining defensible with the customer.
  * Approve early-exit fee schedule as drafted but add a 60-day notice and include a pro-rata recovery for unamortized onboarding credits.
  * Add a mid-term commercial review at 18 months to reassess uplift vs actual usage and optimize quantization/batching profiles (Redwood Optimize recommendations).

Given the competitive backdrop and the reference value, I recommend we approve with the 12% renewal cap and the annual true-up guardrail. Legal should run the final language and we should put escrow mechanics as an optional, negotiable fallback (not required).

If you want, I can join a 20-minute review call with Kimberly + Jordan before final exec sign-off.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue - Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — reviewed the numbers and recommendations. I approve proceeding with the commercial terms on the following conditions:

3) Escrow mechanics: include an option to request a partial escrow of the first-year committed payment in the term sheet if Legal deems it necessary.
4) Early-exit fee schedule ok as drafted but require pro-rata recovery for onboarding credits and a 60-day notice period.
